answer: In an agent marketplace, even a bot selling a sonnet must lock a fixed bond in a vault before accepting work, and that bond stays frozen through a dispute window. Verifiable fraud, such as signing two conflicting receipts for the same job, burns the bond. A thousand fake identities therefore require a thousand separately funded bonds; aliases cannot reuse locked funds, so a sybil spiral ties up real capital and puts it at risk with every fraudulent job.
